name: Operational Inexpressibility License Theory
description: Proves fixed-input languages cannot derive termination verdicts though licensed channels separate systems. Fourteen declared profiles agree yet the verdict distinguishes them.

program.name: The Observation Boundary
program.summary: An observer sends states to records, and its boundary is the set of merged pairs: two distinct states with one record, told apart by no record-determined reading, at infinite resolution cost, repaired by one side symbol whose least alphabet is the largest fiber. The license criterion, under which a target is determined exactly when it is constant on the fibers, is proved on arbitrary sets with its lattice, its Bayes-risk and Blackwell comparison, its Beth gap, the echo law and Shannon's secrecy bound.

oneLine: Fixed-input observation-only languages cannot decide global termination on a shared trace input where fourteen declared profiles coincide, while a proof-backed licensed channel separates the systems.
summary: The theory studies fixed-input languages whose derivable statements factor through a declared observer and whose stored pair shares input and context while colliding on observation and separating dimension and verdict. It asks whether any derivable observation-only statement can constrain or pointwise decide the target and whether licensed side information can restore separation. No derivable statement constrains or decides the target, and the target has no factorization through the observer or its kernel quotient. The concrete KO7 instance uses recursor and self-embedding worlds with a counterfactual witness of equal observations and distinct verdicts. Its fourteen-member declared candidate profile coincides on both systems while the finite termination verdict splits them with no profile decoder. A normalized licensed certificate channel separates the systems with direct residual log 2, licensed residual zero and deficit log 2, and the unified definition makes language-level and observer-level inexpressibility coincide under soundness, completeness and dimension visibility.
boundary: On the licensed side an observer augmented with distinguishing side information factors the target and the certificate channel separates recursor from self-embedding with zero residual. On the direct side derivable observation-only statements are constant on observer fibers and the fourteen-profile observation coincides, so no derivable statement constrains or decides termination. The obstruction is an explicit colliding pair with equal observations and distinct targets at fixed input and shared context. The results locating it are the profile-equality plus collision and no-decoder theorems together with the licensed-separation headline carrying log-2 deficit.

conclusions.statement: The candidate profile on the recursor system coincides with the profile on the self-embedding system, the profile and termination verdict collide on recursor versus self-embedding, and no decoder from candidate profiles recovers the termination verdict on both systems.

Direct profiles are identical with a common fiber and distinct verdicts, the licensed decision separates the systems and agrees with the verdict, direct residual is log 2 with calibration, licensed residual is zero, deficit is log 2, and the soundness license lies outside the declared extractor language.
For every fixed-input boundary and every derivable statement, the statement does not pointwise decide the target on all worlds.
For every fixed-input boundary and every derivable statement, the statement does not constrain the target.
For every fixed-input boundary, the target does not factor through the language observer and has no factorization through the observer-kernel quotient.
There are worlds x and y at the fixed input with same context, equal observations, distinct dimensions and distinct targets.
Under the hypothesis that psi is derivable, psi does not decide the target on both KO7 systems.
The imported termination-verdict statement decides the target pointwise.
The imported termination-verdict statement is not derivable.

Every direct-profile tag has a representative with matching family and non-orientation for both recursor and self-embedding profiles, every inventory row belongs to the combined ledger, row counts are 14, 76 and 90 with nodup and every row present and covered, and the combined artifacts form a closed inventory certificate.
Under hypotheses Sound, Complete and ObserverSeesDimension, LanguageInexpressible holds if and only if ObserverInexpressible holds.
For every fixed-input boundary B, its observed language satisfies ObserverInexpressible via the stored counterfactual pair and satisfies LanguageInexpressible.
For every expression e, it is not the case that e both uses the payload and orients the duplicating step.
The payload target is not licensed by the counter observer.
For every grammar expression orienting the duplicating step, its denotation is licensed by the counter observer.

openPoints: Soundness, completeness and dimension visibility are carried as hypotheses for the language-observer coincidence, with blind, constant-statement and unsound fixtures showing each one is needed.
Derivable statements factor through the observer by a stored field, and the boundary carries a fixed input with a same-context colliding pair.
Direct-grammar separation holds inside the reflected grammar, while outside it the payload-sensitive orienter both reads payload and orients, so the realization hypothesis cannot be dropped.

Licensed separation is proved with a uniform prior and separate calibration facts, and channel separation and rule provenance remain separate conjuncts with the soundness license outside the declared extractor language.
Inventory closure stays inside the declared 14-row plus 76-row ledger, where direct rows carry non-orientation receipts and atlas rows carry classification receipts without measure or order data.

files.summary: Defines certified-forgetting witnesses that orient the duplicating step while violating wrapper sensitivity on both payload coordinates, with dependency-pair and confession-method constructions. Defines a narrow payload operational incompleteness package combining imported witness-threshold bounds with one certified witness. Instantiates the package for KO7 and proves the conjunction of no direct-whole witness, imported-whole truth, first contract admissibility at transformed-call, and existence of a certified witness.
files.conclusion: KO7 exhibits payload-level operational incompleteness with the first admissible contract witness at the transformed-call layer plus one explicit certified-forgetting witness.

files.summary: The file defines the total real weight of a predicate, signed fiber ratios for an observer, the meet cell of two observers and common knowledge as closure under shared fibers. It proves that common knowledge at a state is containment of the meet cell and proves a fiberwise aggregation lemma for saturated cells. It proves that two observers with a common weighting assign equal ratios whenever those assignments are common knowledge at a state whose meet cell has nonzero weight, without positivity or normalization. It gives two finite fixtures showing that nonzero weight and common knowledge are each necessary.
files.conclusion: Two observers with a common weighting and common knowledge of their fiber ratios must agree when the meet cell has nonzero weight, and both hypotheses are necessary.

files.summary: The file defines explicit definition by a derivable denoting statement, the Beth property on a class, and closure under postcomposition. It proves the Padoa direction that explicit definition gives license under soundness and a decomposition of the gap into unlicensed targets and Beth failures. It proves that a complete postcomposition-closed language with nonempty verdicts has the Beth property. It gives fixtures showing soundness, completeness and postcomposition closure are each necessary.
files.conclusion: A sound complete postcomposition-closed language with nonempty verdicts has the Beth property, and completeness and postcomposition closure are each necessary.

files.summary: The file defines orienting targets, the direct grammar as an observed language under a chosen observer, and the projection language of strictly increasing counter functions. It proves the grammar fails the Beth property at the payload-sensitive orienter for the full reading and at the bethGap function for the counter observer. It proves orienting grammar denotations are licensed by the counter and that the projection language is sound and has the Beth property on orienting targets with an explicit-definability equivalence.
files.conclusion: The direct grammar fails the Beth property on orienting targets for both full and counter readings, while the strictly increasing projection language has it.

files.summary: The file defines transport of scopes, constructions and certificates along relation isomorphisms and proves the full semantic profile is invariant under such transport. It computes exact raw and licensed profiles for the Fork3 binary fork with terminal-derived binary witnesses and shows changing the declared repair price changes the profile without changing the relation. It packages forks as presentations and as closed embeddings in ambient systems with transported certificates and terminal counts, realized by a live KO7 instance using kernel steps and SafeStep.
files.conclusion: The raw fork has profile with two terminals and unit repair data and the licensed fork has profile with one terminal and zero repair data, transport preserves profiles, and the same relation admits different prices with full certificates realized in live KO7.

files.summary: The file treats deterministic observers with finite rational priors and point-mass kernels. It proves refinement implies Bayes-risk dominance by composing decoders and proves the converse from risk dominance on two-point priors with the second observer as target, giving an equivalence of the two preorders. It shows a single constant target does not determine refinement via the Bool coordinates. It proves for stochastic models that composition with a rational Markov kernel never lowers Bayes risk.
files.conclusion: For deterministic observers, refinement coincides with uniform Bayes-risk dominance, one target does not suffice, and garbling cannot lower risk.

files.summary: The file defines real finite experiments, decision values, garbling by stochastic matrices and domination across decision problems. It proves garbling lowers every decision value and proves the converse by separating the target experiment from the convex hull of deterministic post-processings. It gives observer, gain-function and zero-one corollaries and controls showing nonempty output is required and that a fully noisy binary experiment is a one-way garbling of the perfect one.
files.conclusion: Domination in all finite decision problems coincides with garbling by a stochastic matrix for nonempty output, restricting to refinement and Bayes-risk order on observers.

files.summary: The file restricts the exhaustive finite side-encoder search by a computable natural-number cost and budget. It proves the returned encoder is feasible and has minimum Bayes side risk among budget-feasible encoders, characterizes emptiness, and proves candidate monotonicity with risk antitonicity in the budget. It gives zero-cost and unit-cost controls showing unconstrained recovery and empty zero-budget search.
files.conclusion: The budgeted search returns a feasible minimum-risk encoder when one exists, with risk antitone in the budget.

files.summary: The file defines padded encodings for naturals, word lists and certificates where the width prefix may announce extra false cells. It proves compact fields decode exactly to padded encodings and that the word decoder accepts only serializations. It proves the strict checker accepts exactly the padded encodings of buildCertificate output and that every accepted bitstring decodes to that certificate. It proves length formulas, canonicality of serializeBits as the unique shortest accepted string, and a padded successor control.
files.conclusion: The strict checker accepts exactly the padded encodings of the constructed certificate, with serializeBits as the unique shortest accepted bitstring.

files.summary: The file defines a small-step bit machine that reads certificate bits one cell per step with width, payload, and halted phases and a consumed-cell counter. It proves a termination measure decreases on every non-halted step and that width, payload, field, and word segments simulate the recursive costed decoders with matching inspection counts. The full run for 3*bits.length+1 steps therefore halts with the recursive parser result, and the parser bitInspections equals the consumed count, with controls for empty and truncated inputs.
files.conclusion: On every input the 3*length+1-step machine run halts with the recursive certificate parser's result and its consumed-cell count equals the parser's bitInspections.

files.summary: The file defines the generic compact codec for natural numbers and word lists, with unary width prefixes, binary payloads, exact length formulas, and decode-encode round trips. It also defines recursive costed parsers that return both the decoded value and the number of inspected bit cells. It proves the costed parsers erase to the accepted parsers, their costs never exceed input length, and successful parses partition the input into consumed prefix plus untouched suffix.
files.conclusion: The compact codec is lossless with exact lengths and its costed parsers count exactly the consumed prefix while never exceeding the input length.

files.summary: The file proves the four asymptotic clauses stated for the canonical trace: trace action over squared depth, proof-entropy fraction with constant c0 plus payload, completed cell-mass share of trace action, and crossover stage over depth. Each limit is obtained from an exact closed-form identity by isolating 1/k corrections or applying squeeze bounds. No new definitions are introduced beyond these limit statements.
files.conclusion: The four trace-law fractions converge to (w+1)/2 over squared depth, i/(i+1), w/(w+1), and 1/(w+1) respectively.

files.summary: The file proves strengthened paper statements not carried by the cited declarations: constancy of license-constant projection families, uniqueness of the record generator bridge and subsingleton LCEL comparison types, a marginal bit-cost identity with geometric lower bound and binary length, opposite explicit-versus-carrier inequalities for large index and index zero, and terminal-record completeness on a sorted model with an unsorted depth-base collision and a quadratic mass bound.
files.conclusion: Positive-depth sorted records are complete for depth, base, and payload with quadratic mass bounded by the confessed burden, while the other strengthened paper inequalities hold under their stated side conditions.

files.summary: The file shows correct comparison of observation pairs through an augmented channel holds exactly when the channel licenses repeat depth. It derives the rank channel for comparison, a lower bound by the largest fiber, a construction from capacity, and a two-sided finite capacity law. Both comparison and recurrence therefore share the same feasible alphabets and the same attained minimum.
files.conclusion: Correct pair comparison and exact repeat-depth recording have the same feasible alphabets with least size maxFiberCard.

files.summary: The file defines confusable pairs, the confusability graph, resolving side channels, and the augmented observer, proving licensing equivalent to proper coloring. It gives exact capacity laws for arbitrary and finite alphabets via fiber target cardinalities, identifies chromatic number with maximum fiber multiplicity and code deficit with its binary logarithm, and tests infinite, growing-fiber, permanent-channel, compactness, and three-pair non-coarsening cases. Finite and infinite examples show attainable and impossible capacities.
files.conclusion: Licensed augmentation equals graph coloring, so the chromatic number is the maximum fiber multiplicity and its binary logarithm is the least resolving code length.

files.summary: This file defines observed languages with language-level inexpressibility and observer-level collision plus soundness, completeness and dimension visibility. It proves the two levels coincide exactly under all three hypotheses and gives the license form of the second clause. It shows each hypothesis is necessary by fixtures dropping one at a time and exhibits joint satisfiability with both levels false and both levels true.
files.conclusion: The file proves that soundness, completeness and dimension visibility jointly make the language-level and observer-level definitions equivalent, with each hypothesis necessary and jointly satisfiable.

files.summary: This file turns every fixed-input language boundary into a sound observed language whose stored pair witnesses the observer level, hence also the language level which coincides with schema operational incompleteness. The KO7 fixed-input language is an instance. It also gives the canonical direct-grammar question in license form, where dependence is counter-unlicensedness and incompleteness follows from counter-licensing of orienting denotations.
files.conclusion: The file proves every fixed-input boundary instantiates the unified definition and the canonical step-argument question does so through the counter license.

files.summary: This file identifies functional dependencies with licenses of restrictions and proves Armstrong soundness and completeness, where two Boolean tuples decide every dependency. It gives universe-polymorphic soundness and completeness via lifts and equivalences and shows one tuple is insufficient. It also proves lists of dependencies are families of licenses, with union and indexed forms as license conjunctions.
files.conclusion: The file proves Armstrong soundness and completeness including universe-polymorphic forms, and that lists of dependencies are exactly families of licenses.

files.summary: This file proves completeness of the dependency-pair method and the Arts and Giesl equivalence between termination, well-founded minimal chains and absence of infinite minimal chains. It develops a bounded presentation where strong normalization is boundedness of reduction lengths and accessibility coincides with bounded runs under finite successors. It shows the bounded matrix is decidable and every free-recursor term has bounded runs.
files.conclusion: The file proves the Arts and Giesl termination equivalence with sequence and bounded-run forms plus decidability and the free-recursor instance.

files.summary: This file studies maximal licensed subsets as repairs, proving consistent answers are fiber-constant states and every state is possible. It proves the repair count is the product of fiber verdict counts and the largest licensed set keeps a most frequent target per fiber. It identifies normalized least deletions with uniform Bayes risk, orders the three Kivinen-Mannila measures, and shows all vanish exactly on licensed pairs with concrete fixtures.
files.conclusion: The file proves repair characterizations, exact repair and fiber counts, the Bayes-risk identity for g3, and vanishing criteria for all three error measures.

files.summary: This file represents reflected-grammar membership by derivation trees and proves no expression both reads the payload and orients the fixed duplicating step. Both sides are inhabited by payload and counter projections, so the separation is non-vacuous. It transfers the boundary to denotational subgrammars and shows the realization premise is necessary via an outside-grammar payload-sensitive orienter.
files.conclusion: The file proves the non-vacuous direct-grammar separation with transfer to denotational subgrammars and necessity of the transfer hypothesis.

files.summary: This file restates payload blindness as licensing by the counter observer on the canonical carrier. It proves every orienting grammar denotation is counter-licensed with transfer to denotational subgrammars, while the payload target is unlicensed by an explicit collision. Outside the grammar the orientation-to-license implication fails via the payload-sensitive orienter.
files.conclusion: The file proves the direct-grammar boundary is exactly the counter-license instance with an explicit collision and outside-grammar failure.

files.summary: This file states the equality-guarded KO7 positional repair built from a selection of constructor positions. It proves the repair freezes the equality-witness position, retains every requested non-equality position, closes recursive-context selection under both application positions, is confluent, and is the least such confluent extension. It also shows selecting only the recursive-context position does not ensure confluence.
files.conclusion: The equality-guarded positional repair is the least confluent extension preserving requested non-equality positions, while the recD-only selection is not confluent.

files.summary: This file implements the license criterion, observer refinement, collision search, and target-kernel partition as computations over an explicit complete enumeration of the source. Each executable is proved sound and complete against its propositional notion: true answers coincide with licensing or refinement, and the search returns a colliding pair exactly when licensing fails. Controls include the empty and one-point carriers, where every target is licensed, and the parity fixture on two Booleans.
files.conclusion: Executable checks decide licensing and refinement, and search certifies failure with an explicit collision.

files.summary: This file gives a deterministic synthesis of an optimal resolving side channel for finite inputs from an explicit enumeration. It orders target values by first appearance in each observer fiber, uses the local rank as code, proves resolving and licensing, proves optimality with no smaller Fin alphabet, and gives a fixed-width binary codec. It also synthesizes a channel at the computed stabilization stage that remains licensing for all dynamic orbit stages.
files.conclusion: Local-rank synthesis yields an optimal resolving channel attaining fiber-multiplicity capacity and permanent licensing from the stabilization stage.

files.summary: This file classifies rank functions in every faithful realization of the free recursor. Generated root steps and transformed calls each admit infinitely many full strict orders via parameterized rank families. Among transformed-call ranks, those constant on counter fibers are exactly strictly increasing recodings of the counter, and their full-order quotient has one class.
files.conclusion: Every faithful realization has infinitely many rank-order classes for root and call steps, yet counter-determined ranks have exactly one order class.

files.summary: This file defines faithful realizations as signature algebras with injective fold and realizes root, call and contextual steps as images of free relations. It transports well-foundedness, determinism, confluence, machines, orbits and witness hierarchies through closed embeddings. It shows the KO7 constructor interpretation realizes exactly the two recursor rules, gives collapsed and escaping counterexamples, and exhibits construction and confession responses on the KO7 schema.
files.conclusion: Faithful injective realizations transport well-foundedness, determinism, confluence and machines, but reflection without outgoing closure does not suffice for ambient termination.

files.summary: This file specializes the generic fiber-capacity theory to the two-role fixture and Fork3. The value observer collapsing both roles has fiber multiplicity two and deficit one bit, the role coordinate closes the deficit, the two roles collide for value-only reading, and the deficit equals the zero-evidence overproduction gap of Fork3.
files.conclusion: The two-role fixture has multiplicity two and deficit one bit, closed by the role channel and equal to the Fork3 zero-evidence gap.

files.summary: This file develops finite observer-target fiber capacity with no rewrite-system dependency. It defines realized target sets, their maximum size, and the ceiling-log deficit, proves zero deficit is factorization and positive deficit is a collision, and proves tight lower bounds. It constructs an optimal side channel with exactly multiplicity symbols and shows deficit bits are both sufficient and minimal, with monotonicity under kernel refinement.
files.conclusion: Fiber multiplicity is the exact minimum side-alphabet size and its ceiling log is the exact minimum fixed-length bit width.

files.summary: This file bounds conditional Shannon entropy by the logarithm of fiber multiplicity for finite sources with a prior, observer and target. It proves the bound in nats and bits, characterizes zero entropy as licensing on the support, and characterizes equality as full uniform fibers. Controls show a nonuniform fiber lies strictly below the bound and a zero-mass collision leaves entropy at zero.
files.conclusion: Conditional Shannon entropy is bounded by log fiber multiplicity with equality exactly for full uniform fibers and zero exactly for support licensing.

files.summary: This file defines executable Boolean procedures over explicitly enumerated finite relation tables for reachability, normality, joinability, source confluence, path reconstruction, nonjoinability witnesses, defect filtering, repair-cover optimization and bounded witness-rank search. It proves each procedure sound and complete against reflexive-transitive closure and the noncomputable cover and rank references under the same enumeration. It adds semantic peak inputs, first-order critical-pair origins and a finite adapter that transfers finite nonjoinability to term rewriting, plus controls showing auxiliary prices, coverage and adequacy are not fixed by relation data.
files.conclusion: All finite reachability, normality, joinability, confluence, path, nonjoinability, repair-cover and bounded-rank queries are decided soundly and completely relative to the supplied enumeration, and finite nonjoinability transfers to represented term rewriting while auxiliary coordinates remain independent of the relation table.

files.summary: This file builds joint and observation-mass models for finite rational parametric families with a rational prior. It proves that equal posteriors on positive-mass samples coincide with proportional likelihoods. It proves sufficiency equals Fisher-Neyman factorization under a strictly positive prior and that the posterior map is minimal sufficient, plus a two-point fixture showing full support is required.
files.conclusion: For full-support priors, sufficiency is factorization and the posterior map is minimal sufficient, while full support is necessary.

files.summary: This file proves pigeonhole recurrence for finite observers and shows the first repeat occurs by card Q with earlier stages new. It proves no memoryless function of the current observation determines repeat status, with a parity-orbit instance, and characterizes compatible observers by unique image dynamics with eventual periodicity and kernel and license stabilization by card Q minus one. It refutes persistence without compatibility via a power-of-two observer and proves sharpness by countdown examples plus finite-attained-image generalizations.
files.conclusion: Finite observers always recur within the pigeonhole bound and compatible licenses stabilize by that bound sharply, but memoryless repeat detection and eventual periodicity are impossible in general.

files.summary: This module packages finite probability masses with nonnegativity and total-mass-one laws and finite-output conditional kernels normalized at every input. It provides row, deterministic and fair-binary constructions and computes the fair-binary entropy as log 2. It defines typed finite channels with source prior, target, observation and normalized posterior rows plus prior-weighted residual entropy, without imposing Bayes consistency.
files.conclusion: Finite distributions, kernels, deterministic and fair-binary examples, and typed finite channels with normalized rows and prior-weighted residual entropy are packaged with the fair-binary entropy equal to log 2.

files.summary: This file defines computable finite root and one-step reduct sets for finite first-order systems by matching left-hand sides and rewriting one argument. It proves the root and full reduct membership statements are sound and complete for the rewrite relation when right-hand-side variables are contained in left-hand-side variables. It shows the condition is required by exhibiting one rule with infinitely many variable reducts.
files.conclusion: Finite first-order systems satisfying the variable condition are finitely branching with an exact finite reduct set, and the condition is sharp.

files.summary: This module packages fixed-input languages whose derivable statements factor through a declared observer and whose distinguished pair fixes input and context while colliding observations and separating dimensions and targets. It proves derivable denotations factor through observation and hence cannot constrain or decide the target, and the target has no observer or quotient factorization. It bridges this semantic boundary to the legacy abstract operational-incompleteness predicate.
files.conclusion: No derivable observation-only statement constrains or decides the target, and the target has no factorization through the observer or its kernel quotient.

files.summary: The file defines the free recursor root relation with zero and successor rules and the transformed-call dependency-pair relation on closed recursor syntax, together with executable next-step functions and an extractor that recovers the callee from a successor step. It proves soundness and completeness of extraction and that both relations are deterministic, well-founded, and confluent with exact rank and cost functions. It classifies extensions of the root relation, showing extraction completeness holds exactly for compatible extras, equivalently for pair-free new edges, and exhibits counterexamples for wrong right-hand sides and repeated rules.
files.conclusion: Every root extension is extraction-complete exactly when its genuinely new edges never share a source with a dependency pair.

files.summary: The file builds a boundary kernel with source, callee, and output terms and locates the generator at two output paths for frame and active roles. It defines the actual Boolean channel comparing each branch to the extracted call and proves it separates roles exogenously while refusing value factorization and unit collapse. It identifies the uniform channel evidence with the binary role-resolving channel, computes one spent bit, and extends deficit, gap, and joint-posterior factorization to arbitrary binary role laws.
files.conclusion: The extracted call yields an exogenous Boolean channel that no value-only function can reproduce and that carries exactly one bit, with joint factorization for arbitrary binary role laws.

files.summary: The file defines counter and payload observations, profile measures, direct whole witnesses in a reflected grammar, imported natural rankings, transformed-call witnesses, and counter-erasing signature decoders. It proves every successor profile occurs, no direct witness orients all steps, the executable derivation height is the least imported ranking and is not profile-factored, and no erased-counter decoder exists. It builds truth and boundary witness hierarchies whose adequate depths are exactly at least one and at least two, giving representation-shift bottlenecks at depths one and two.
files.conclusion: Truth needs depth one and the counter-erasing boundary needs depth two, with no direct whole witness.

files.summary: The file defines the injective map from closed four-constructor free terms to seven-constructor recursor terms preserving zero, successor, wrap, and recur. It proves the map preserves delta-prefix length, counter and payload observations, and profile measures, and that root steps correspond exactly forward and backward from the image. It defines the least root height on free terms, proves exact decrease, zero characterization, pointwise leastness, non-factorization through profiles, and equality with derivationHeight on closed images.
files.conclusion: The four-constructor root theory embeds faithfully in the seven-constructor recursor theory with identical steps, profiles, and least root height.

files.summary: The file records fixtures showing hypotheses of the package theorems cannot be dropped, with most fixtures beside their theorems. It adds a three-state rotation read by the zero test whose orbit-observer kernels do not stabilize, the naturals under constant observation whose infinite fiber admits no finite side channel, and an empty certificate task whose capacity search returns none. It conjoins twenty-five fixture statements grouped as fifteen necessity items, excluding the duplicated-target product control which carries no distinctness hypothesis.
files.conclusion: Every listed hypothesis is necessary, witnessed by an explicit fixture where hypothesis and conclusion fail together.

files.summary: The file represents two operational tasks by a product target and proves joint licensing is exactly the conjunction of component licenses. It shows separately sufficient side labels compose by product while the exact finite minimum is the realized joint fiber multiplicity. A constant-observer Boolean example with duplicated targets has joint multiplicity two rather than four, so the product of separate minima strictly overcounts.
files.conclusion: Joint minimum side-alphabet size is the realized joint fiber multiplicity, which can be strictly below the product of separate minima.

files.summary: The file closes the union of fourteen proof-bearing direct-profile families and the separate 76-row termination method atlas without conflating them. It proves each direct tag has a concrete candidate with relation-correct non-orientation for both the root and self-embedding relations and each atlas family has an exact non-residual classification receipt. It forms the 90-row disjoint ledger, proves length, nodup, completeness, branch disjointness, exact U6 counts, total coverage, and a propositional closeout certificate.
files.conclusion: All 14 direct-profile rows have relation-correct non-orientation receipts and all 76 atlas rows have exact non-residual classification receipts, totaling 90 disjoint covered rows.

files.summary: The file builds a concrete fixed-input language with two derivable observation-only constants and one non-derivable imported termination-verdict statement over a common KO7 trace input. It instantiates the generic boundary with recursor and self-embedding worlds that share context and complete candidate profile yet differ in system dimension and termination verdict. It proves the fixed-input counterfactual, that no derivable statement decides termination, that the imported verdict would decide it but is not derivable, and that derivability is nonempty.
files.conclusion: With common input and observation but different systems and verdicts, no derivable observation-only statement decides termination while the non-derivable imported verdict would.

files.summary: The file builds a normalized channel on the two recursor and self-embedding systems with uniform prior, full-profile direct observation with fair posterior, and a proof-backed licensed decision from transformed-call and license certificates. It proves the direct profile collides while verdicts differ, the licensed decision separates without inspecting the verdict, and both posteriors are calibrated. It computes fair cell entropy log 2 versus licensed entropy zero, residuals log 2 versus zero, deficit log 2, headline composition, and nonvacuity.
files.conclusion: The licensed certificate channel separates the two systems with deficit log 2 while the direct profile cannot, without inspecting the verdict to decide.

files.summary: The file builds the complete meta-observer over an explicit fourteen-constructor declared universe with concrete linear, max, pair, vector and lex witnesses. It defines relation-relative orientation and proves every declared candidate orients neither the terminating KO7 Step nor SelfEmbeddingStep. It then shows the full candidate profile coincides on the two systems while the finite strong-normalization verdict splits, giving operational inexpressibility and no profile decoder.
files.conclusion: The fourteen-family declared profile agrees on both actual relations yet the finite termination verdict distinguishes them, yielding operational inexpressibility with no profile decoder.

files.summary: The file instantiates the schema-generic operational-incompleteness predicate on the reflected direct-measure grammar at the payload coordinate pi_y. It defines the canonical counter-payload carrier and the complete positive-copy duplicating relation and proves global orientation equivalent to the earlier duplicating-root predicate. The payload projection witnesses dimension use without orientation while the counter witnesses orientation without dimension use, giving a non-vacuous incompleteness theorem.
files.conclusion: The reflected direct grammar at the step-argument dimension is operationally incomplete for global orientation of the fixed duplicating-carrier system.

files.summary: The file defines kept mass for guessing within a list and k-try vulnerability as summed suprema over menus of at most k values. It proves the repair frontier equals total weight minus vulnerability, with normalized and Bayes-risk forms. It proves concavity in k, the exact-size supremum form under nonnegativity, and a two-state uniform computation.
files.conclusion: The repair frontier equals total weight minus k-try vulnerability, with exact-size form, concavity, and a computed two-state uniform example.

files.summary: The file defines the license as observer-kernel inclusion and refinement as factorization of the coarse observer through the fine one. It proves factorization through the attained image with a unique decoder, full decoders under nonempty codomain with an empty-source control, and failure as collision. It characterizes refinement by license-theory inclusion including Boolean and fixed-target forms, and proves licenses are lost at most once along coarsenings with first-loss existence, uniqueness, witnesses and dichotomy.
files.conclusion: Licensing is kernel inclusion with attained-image decoders, refinement is license-theory inclusion, and coarsening loses license at most once with an exact cutoff.

files.summary: The file supplies recursor instances of the generic license theory with the counter, residual-work and payload coordinates on finite traces. It shows the counter is injective hence licenses every target while the constant observer fails for payload with an explicit collision. It proves rank computes dependency-pair cost and licenses it but not the erased payload, and analyzes payload-governed loop extensions where rank licenses termination exactly when no payload loops, ending in a scope dichotomy.
files.conclusion: On one carrier the counter licenses base termination and costs but fails after a payload-sensitive loop extension that retains every base step.

files.summary: The module separates finite-choice Hartley complexity of W1 construction witnesses from Shannon role information on the W2 confession side. It proves W1 Hartley unbounded through injective orienting families of full Step and the active-flag entropy at most one bit with equality at binary arity. It proves the chain rule recovering full role Hartley from flag plus residual frame term and packages the heterogeneous profile.
files.conclusion: Construction choice is unbounded while confession active-flag entropy is at most one bit, with full role Hartley recovered by the residual term.

files.summary: The file sends an equivalence kernel to its Boolean licensed targets and a target family to its common kernel, proving the antitone Galois law. Boolean class indicators reconstruct every setoid exactly, giving injectivity, idempotent closure with fixed-point classification, and non-strict and strict refinement as reverse inclusion. It packages the complete Galois correspondence with kernel reconstruction for observer license theories.
files.conclusion: Kernels and Boolean license families form a Galois connection with exact reconstruction, idempotent closure, and strict refinement as strict reverse inclusion.

files.summary: The file treats observer kernels as equivalence relations with refinement and licensing as inclusions. Every relation is the kernel of its quotient map, so observers modulo kernel are order-isomorphic to setoids and partitions. The joint observer gives the infimum kernel and the common coarsening the supremum with an EqvGen chain description, and license theories meet and join accordingly with parity as strictness control.
files.conclusion: Observers modulo kernel are the partition lattice with joint infimum and coarsening supremum governing license theories, strictly separated by parity.

files.summary: The file defines the stabilizer of permutations preserving each observer value with fiber transpositions. It proves licensed targets are exactly stabilizer invariants, fibers are stabilizer orbits, refinement is subgroup inclusion with kernel equality as stabilizer equality, and injectivity as trivial stabilizer. It gives the fiber-product decomposition with factorial counting and a two-point example where observer symmetry strictly exceeds named-constant automorphisms.
files.conclusion: Licensing, fibers, refinement and injectivity are exactly stabilizer invariance, orbits, inclusion and triviality with fiber-product structure, not language automorphisms.

files.summary: This file defines licensing on retained sets, correctness sets of decoders, maximal licensed sets, fiber-attained decoders, refused weight, menus and the repair frontier. It proves that every collision is either separated by a side channel or refused, that licensed sets are exactly decoder correctness sets, and that maximal ones correspond to fiber-attained decoders. It proves the least refusal equals the Bayes risk, the least lift equals the fiber multiplicity, and the frontier interpolates from total weight to Bayes risk to zero with diminishing returns.
files.conclusion: The k-symbol repair frontier starts at total weight, equals Bayes risk at one symbol, vanishes exactly from the fiber multiplicity on, is antitone with diminishing returns, and every collision forces lift or refusal with both repairs non-unique.

files.summary: This file instantiates lift-or-refuse on the free recursor role gate and the diagonal guard. The dependency-pair channel is a least two-symbol lift of the role collision with refusal cost one half, while the blind pair observer has diagonal versus off-diagonal maximal refusals. The diagonal needs one side bit that exists abstractly but no Sigma void test supplies, yielding disequality inexpressibility and the SafeStep guard as the off-diagonal refusal.
files.conclusion: The recursor role takes the lift via the dependency-pair channel with least two symbols while the diagonal guard takes the refusal with diagonal versus off-diagonal maximal sets and no Sigma void-test lift.

files.summary: This file proves the universal property of the lift and the absence of a universal refusal. Every observer refining q and licensing P refines their joint observer, which has the meet kernel. A greatest retained set on which q licenses P exists exactly when q licenses P, so no collision admits a greatest refusal.
files.conclusion: The joint observer is the greatest licensing refinement, but no greatest licensed retained set exists at any collision.

files.summary: This file defines finite rational observation models, joints, marginals, derived posteriors, and the executable 0-1 Bayes decoder and risk by finite maximization. It proves Bayes optimality against deterministic and randomized decoders and the deterministic and randomized data-processing inequalities. It characterizes zero Bayes risk as licensing on joint support and exhibits the zero-mass collision where support purity holds without full-carrier licensing.
files.conclusion: The executable Bayes decoder is optimal among deterministic and randomized decoders, post-processing cannot improve it, and zero Bayes error characterizes support licensing rather than full-carrier licensing.

files.summary: This file defines normal-form faithful simulations and proves transfer of unique reachable normals and unique normals under conversion. It proves termination transport through stuttering simulations with lexicographic descent. Fork collapse and loop-versus-empty controls show injectivity on normals and stutter descent are each necessary.
files.conclusion: Normal-form uniqueness and termination transfer through faithful simulations, while injectivity on normals and stutter descent are each necessary as shown by fork and loop controls.

files.summary: This file defines the kernel Setoid of an observer, its quotient type with canonical projection and descended observer, kernel-respecting functions with a universal factor, and finite distributions with deterministic pushforward plus Shannon and Hartley functionals. It proves quotient equality coincides with observer equality, that every kernel-respecting function factors through the projection with a unique factor, and that pointwise-equal channels share pushforwards. It further proves pushforward, Shannon and Hartley quantities are preserved by the quotient factorization and exhibits a four-state parity observer that identifies even states while separating even from odd.
files.conclusion: Any function constant on observer fibers factors uniquely through the kernel quotient, preserving finite pushforward, Shannon and Hartley quantities.

files.summary: This module defines verdict determination, collisions, fiber constancy and quotient factorization. It proves decoders imply fiber constancy, converse with inhabited verdicts or surjective observers, and quotient factorization equivalent to fiber constancy with failure exactly equivalent to a collision. The empty-world fixture has fiber constancy and no collision yet no total decoder.
files.conclusion: Decoder existence, fiber constancy and quotient factorization coincide up to inhabitance or surjectivity, with collisions as exact obstructions and the empty world showing why inhabitance is needed.

files.summary: This file defines the observer-quotient step and system generated by representative edges and the canonical licensed projection. It proves the projection maps length-indexed paths to quotient paths of equal length and preserves reachability. A two-valued observer on the chain fixture shows the genuine edge survives in the quotient.
files.conclusion: Every admitted source path maps to a quotient path of the same length, hence reachability is preserved forward, as witnessed by the chain fixture.

files.summary: The file defines three trace coordinates for a duplicating trace and their step values, with the counter given by trace_ctr, the stack by trace_wraps and the copies by trace_pay. It shows the frame slot and the active-site slot of record terms both take the generator token gen, and combines these facts with emission and preservation to exhibit two distinct generator positions in the primitive duplicator right-hand side. It shows two distinct indices yield two distinct points of the progress-licensed quotient, giving nontriviality of the quotient from nontriviality of the index set. It shows the guarded step from eqW void void has void as its single reduct, giving guarded local joinability there.
files.conclusion: Together the file establishes the four paper clauses: counter uniqueness, the generator-token bridge with two distinct generator positions, nontriviality of the progress quotient, and guarded local joinability at eqW void void.

files.summary: This file defines injective indexed orbit systems with progress observations, generated steps, and progress quotients identifying equal indices. It proves index relations are isomorphic to generated and quotient steps. On recursor terms, increasing indices are converse to transformed calls and isomorphic to wrapper expansion, finite countdowns match bounded prefixes, yet no infinite forward-call execution and no wrap-to-call simulation exist.
files.conclusion: Increasing recursor indices are converse to transformed calls and match finite wrapper prefixes, yet infinite wrapper expansion cannot be simulated by forward calls.

files.summary: The file defines root steps for the r-ary duplicator and a same-input checker over shared certificate syntax. The base rule rewrites F x y Z to x and the step rule rewrites F x y (S n) to G (replicate r y) (F x y n). It proves the checker is sound and that canonical zero and successor certificates are accepted. It proves a strict compact binary certificate exists exactly for r-ary root steps, and for F-headed sources exactly for duplicator steps, while G-headed sources admit no such certificate.
files.conclusion: For every arity r, strict compact binary certificates exist exactly for r-ary root steps and never for G-framed sources.

files.summary: The file defines a finite certificate syntax with rule tag, occurrence path, projection argument and two ranks, plus prefix-free serialization and a total deserializer. It defines a same-input Boolean checker that recomputes structural equalities and rank decrease without trusting claimed values. It proves the checker agrees with declarative meaning, is sound for free-recursion root steps, and is complete via an executable constructor that also survives faithful realizations. It lifts checking to serialized words and compact strict binary messages, proves existence of a strict binary certificate is equivalent to the root-step relation, and separates the serialized cost from an older assembly-cost formula.
files.conclusion: Strict compact binary certificates exist exactly for free-recursion root steps, with checked constructions that survive every faithful realization.

files.summary: The file proves closed forms for the unary duplicator cumulative mass, including that twice the mass at height one equals beta times (k+1)(k+2). It derives the exact ratio of that mass to k squared and shows the ratio tends to beta over two as k grows. It also proves that the inefficiency coefficient at odd index 2N+1 is at least N when payload weight is at least one.
files.conclusion: The unary mass-to-square ratio tends to half the payload size, and odd-index inefficiency grows at least linearly.

files.summary: The file proves that the schema step rule adds one frame and removes one successor layer from the counter. It shows frame count rises by one on each recursive firing of the canonical orbit, never decreases through the terminal base step, and that counter plus frames equals depth. It proves payload mass grows at least linearly with stage while the counter drops, and exhibits a base-rule case where payload frames leave with the erased argument.
files.conclusion: Each recursive firing adds one frame while removing one counter layer, with frames monotone along the canonical trace except for payload frames erased by the base rule.

files.summary: The file defines common witnesses for observer fibers and decoders on the observer quotient for set-valued admissibility. It proves quotient recovery exists exactly when every fiber has a common witness, and that a conflicting pair refutes recovery. It shows pairwise compatibility follows from a common witness but does not imply it via a three-state fixture, embeds function-valued targets as singleton admissibility, and shows a constant-false decoder language can fail despite complete information.
files.conclusion: Quotient set-valued recovery holds exactly with fiber common witnesses, while pairwise compatibility and restricted languages do not suffice.

files.summary: The file defines fiber colorings where each nonempty color class shares an admissible certificate and proves a k-symbol side channel exists exactly when every fiber is k-colorable. It defines fiber chromatic numbers and their maximum as exact capacity, proving a side channel exists exactly above capacity and that singleton targets recover fiber multiplicity. It gives an exhaustive executable search returning least feasible alphabet or none, and shows the three-state fixture has capacity two with two colors succeeding and one failing.
files.conclusion: The least side alphabet equals the maximum fiber chromatic number, two on the three-state fixture.

files.summary: The file defines observer/color cells, common witnesses on sets, and partial decoders defined only on realized pairs. It proves a partial decoder exists exactly when every realized cell has a common witness, equivalently when every bad fiber subset without a common certificate is non-monochromatic. It exhibits a three-state fixture where every pair shares a certificate yet one side symbol fails while two symbols succeed.
files.conclusion: Set-valued side channels are exactly fiber-hypergraph colorings, with the three-state case separating pairwise compatibility from two-color necessity.

files.summary: The file defines observation fibers, prior repeats, repeat depth as prior-repeat count, repeat status, and largest fiber size for finite-horizon observers. It proves depth values on a size-k fiber are exactly 0 to k-1, so target multiplicity equals largest fiber size and deficit equals its binary ceiling logarithm, attained by a rank channel. It classifies repeat status multiplicity and bit cost as zero/one for injective observers and one/two for noninjective ones, derives ceiling-average pigeonhole lower bounds, and proves no fixed finite side alphabet licenses exact depth at every horizon via the constant observer.
files.conclusion: Largest fiber size gives exact depth cost and rank-channel optimality, status costs zero or one bit by injectivity, and no fixed finite alphabet works at all horizons.

files.summary: This file defines rule-determined data families, imported data witnesses, and proof-valued soundness licenses. It extracts the actual KO7 rec_succ dependency pair with its singleton call graph and projection coordinate, certifies it, and shows renaming equivariance. It shows construction-rank selection and license availability are imported and hence not rule-determined, and supplies a concrete instance-level license from transformed to source termination.
files.conclusion: The concrete KO7 pair extraction is rule-determined with renaming invariance, while construction-rank choice and license availability are imported and not rule-determined, with a concrete proof-valued bridge to source termination.

files.summary: This file proves finite entropy laws for deterministic role partitions with explicit handling of zero-mass cells. Role entropy splits into partition-label entropy plus conditional within-cell entropy, in nats and in bits. The nonuniform active-versus-frame specialization spends exactly the binary entropy of the active mass and leaves frame-mass-weighted frame entropy, vanishing at the endpoints and for a single frame.
files.conclusion: Every finite deterministic partition splits role entropy into spent label entropy plus residual within-cell entropy, with the active-frame case spending exactly the binary entropy of the active mass.

files.summary: This file lifts partition entropy to arbitrary finite carriers, licensed-channel deficit, and overproduction gap. Mixing partition conditionals reconstructs the law and identifies deficit with spent label entropy. The r-ary dependency-pair channel is identified with the active-frame partition, with uniform spent and residual formulas and zero gap for binary one-frame.
files.conclusion: Deterministic partitions realize the licensed deficit as spent bits and the r-ary dependency-pair channel is the active-frame partition, with zero gap in the binary one-frame case.

files.summary: This file builds a generic rule-invariant Galois connection for an arbitrary rule-indexed relation. Rule families and predicate families determine each other by one-step preservation, with antitone maps, idempotent closures, and singleton and family repairs. Deleting violators gives the greatest preserving subfamily and least exclusion, which partition the request.
files.conclusion: Rule families and invariant families form an antitone Galois connection whose repair is the greatest preserving subfamily with least exclusion partitioning the request.

files.summary: This file proves the first-sufficient-horizon dichotomy for retained observation histories and the coarsest licensing memory. Licensing persists to longer horizons, so either no horizon licenses or exactly those above a unique first horizon do. The revealing observer first licenses the Boolean identity at one and the forgetting observer from zero, with the target-kernel quotient as coarsest memory.
files.conclusion: Retained histories admit a unique first licensing horizon, realized at one by the revealing observer and at zero by the forgetting observer, with the target-kernel quotient as coarsest licensing memory.

files.summary: This file defines finite retained observation histories and proves refinement and licensing monotonicity. A history refines every stage it contains and longer histories refine shorter ones, so stage licensing transports to histories. The forgetting control shows current observation can lose the Boolean identity while the retained two-stage history keeps it.
files.conclusion: Retained histories preserve licensing monotonically, so the forgetting observer history still licenses what its current stage forgets.

files.summary: This file proves the finite-horizon Snell envelope for stopping models. Bellman values dominate stopping and every continuation, hence are the least excessive majorant. Where value differs from stopping value an attaining continuation exists, and stopping exactly at equality attains the value.
files.conclusion: Bellman values are the least excessive majorant and are attained by stopping exactly when value equals stopping value.

files.summary: This file defines sound Boolean verdicts and their weighted output laws. At an instance where the property holds every sound verdict returns true, so the output is a point mass with zero Shannon entropy. Since the free recursor terminates, this applies to termination verdicts at the recursor.
files.conclusion: Every finite family of sound verdicts has zero-entropy output at any holding instance, in particular termination verdicts at the free recursor.

files.summary: This file instantiates sufficiency with full observation as the deterministic identity model. Sufficiency there means constancy on positive-prior fibers, coinciding with licensing under full support and with Bayes-risk attainment. The target-kernel quotient is the coarsest sufficient observer, while the fully noisy binary identity and the empty world separate sufficiency from joint-support licensing and definability.
files.conclusion: The target-kernel quotient is the coarsest sufficient observer, with stochastic separation and empty-verdict failure as sharp limits.

files.summary: This file constructs finite adapters for rewrite systems whose rules rewrite one nullary symbol to another, with step and reachability matching the symbol graph. The fork with s to a and b and both to c joins a and b, while the table observed without c has no common reduct and admits no adapter. The one-rule orbit f of x to f of S of x admits no finite adapter realizing any f of t.
files.conclusion: Every constant TRS has a finite adapter, while the observed fork and the infinite orbit give sharp no-adapter controls.

files.summary: This file builds the canonical quotient of states by equality of target values. Any licensed observer refines this quotient and the quotient itself is licensed, giving the coarsest sufficient observer unique up to kernel. Joint observers give least common refinements and family licensing, with Boolean coordinates and a parity fixture showing non-vacuity.
files.conclusion: The target-kernel quotient is the unique-up-to-kernel coarsest licensed observer, with joint observers as least common refinements.

files.summary: Defines integer dot product, coordinate increments and affine readings of finite coordinate observations, with constancy from a source and annihilation of reachable increments. Proves a relation-generic criterion: a reading is constant on all states reachable from a source iff its coefficients annihilate every reachable transition increment, and classifies agreement of two readings by initial equality plus annihilation by the coefficient difference. Builds an executable checker over a duplicate-free enumeration that searches for a reachable violating edge and proves it sound and complete against the generic criterion. Specializes to binary and arbitrary-arity recursor orbits, recovering trace conservation and trace-equivalence classifications and showing abstract coordinates equal readings of actual r-ary execution terms.
files.conclusion: An affine observation is conserved from a source exactly when its coefficients annihilate every reachable transition increment, decidable by a finite checker and classified as k=0 or a=r·b+c on r-ary orbits.

files.summary: The file builds truth-level and boundary-relative witness hierarchies for the KO7 termination predicate and proves they realize representation-shift bottlenecks at depths one and two respectively, with sharp wrong-depth failures on either side. It then builds proof-carrying layers and a constant Nat-to-unit layer interface satisfying the unit law. That interface is many-to-one with no left inverse, fails canonical preservation of isZeroState, yet supports a sound transport of belowSuccessor, so property soundness does not yield faithful state reconstruction.
files.conclusion: KO7 termination realizes the truth-level bottleneck at depth one and the boundary-relative bottleneck at depth two with sharp wrong-depth failures, while a constant Nat-to-unit interface shows property transport coexists with noninjective abstraction.

files.summary: This file defines abstract witness hierarchies with accepted witnesses and minimal-order relations. It defines single-layer bottlenecks as true properties first witnessed at depth k, with upper- and lower-bound corollaries. It defines interface bottlenecks across two-layer towers with empty lower and witnessed higher layers plus transfer. It packages a decidable-instance pre-undecidability fracture without claiming an undecidability boundary.
files.conclusion: Bottlenecks are characterized as true properties with no adequate witness below k but one at k, lifted to cross-layer interface form.

files.summary: This file composes state interfaces and backward property implications along finite chains. It composes witness transports under intermediate realization and propagates accepted certificates through prefix states. It proves cross-layer transfer, semantic transfer, prefix transfer, and an endpoint bottleneck from an interior gap. It shows soundness alone need not realize and implications alone need not transport, with axiom checks.
files.conclusion: Interfaces and property transfers compose along chains, and an interior witness gap induces an endpoint interface bottleneck while soundness alone realizes nothing.

files.summary: This file packages abstract semantic layers with transitions and witness families. It externalizes verifiers with soundness and defines adequate witnesses with a soundness corollary. It defines abstraction and concretization maps with a unit-only layer interface weaker than a Galois connection. It defines witness transport, canonical abstracted properties, and two-layer towers with extractors.
files.conclusion: Layers, interfaces with unit condition, and sound witness transport are packaged with canonical abstracted properties and tower extractors.

files.summary: This file connects the abstract bottleneck framework to the concrete KO7 stack. It defines KO7 termination and property-fixed witness families at direct, imported-whole, transformed-call, and external depths. It proves a truth-level bottleneck at depth one via polynomial and MPO witnesses with none at zero. It proves a boundary-relative bottleneck at depth two via dependency pairs, with WitnessOrder bridges and a decidable termination instance.
files.conclusion: KO7 exhibits a truth-level bottleneck at depth one and a boundary-relative bottleneck at depth two via dependency pairs.

files.summary: Defines an abstract operational question interface and the predicate for being operationally incomplete, plus a direct-aggregation claim language for step-duplicating systems. Proves the direct-aggregation language is incomplete once the dimension is present, using additive, transparent-compositional and unbounded-affine barriers, and packages a concrete evidence bundle from any projection rank. Separates construction methods from confession methods and shows no response can be both, with both classes inhabited on the free schema by W1 and the counter-depth projection. Adds a projection-transaction reading of the boundary as a static map from trace to verdict.
files.conclusion: The direct-aggregation language is operationally incomplete, projection ranks yield the exact incompleteness bundle, and construction and confession responses are disjoint yet both inhabited on the free schema.

files.summary: This file is a reach and axiom audit for the AumannAgreement module. It checks mass, fiber-ratio and probability assignments, meet cells and common knowledge, and Aumann agreement theorems with their required hypotheses. It also checks counterexamples showing positive mass and common knowledge are each required.
files.conclusion: Common knowledge with positive mass forces agreement, and each hypothesis is shown necessary.

files.summary: This file gives full reach and axiom coverage for the BethDefinabilityInstances module. It checks the orienting class, grammar and projection languages, the Beth gap object with its orienting and non-denotability facts, and the projection Beth property with its explicit-definability equivalence. It proves no new content.

files.summary: This file gives full reach and axiom coverage for the BethDefinability framework. It checks explicit definability, Beth property on a class, postcomposition closure and licensing lemmas, plus constant-function and identity-statement counterexamples. It proves no new content.

files.summary: This file checks declaration, axiom and semantic-instance content for the binary-fork exact profile. It verifies raw and licensed transport data, exact semantic profiles, repair-cost separation on the same relation, adequacy certificates, prefix codes and KO7 ambient instances with two terminals. Examples execute the exact-profile equalities, rank computations and terminal counts.

files.summary: This file is a permanent reach and axiom audit for the BlackwellOrder module. It checks deterministic models, simulating decoders, Bayes-risk monotonicity under refinement, half-half priors, two-point and self characterizations of refinement, and garbling constructions. It proves no new content.

files.summary: This file is a reach and axiom check for the BlackwellStochastic module. It checks real experiments, garbling versus dominance, convex-hull constructors, observer and rational experiments, gain vulnerability, and noisy binary experiments. It also checks that nonempty output is required and that noisy garbles perfect but not conversely.

It adds thirteen evaluated examples including parity licensing, impossibility for identity, infinite chromatic number and stagewise without common channels.

files.summary: This file checks the executable transition-conservation surface. It runs paired checks on readings, constancy, agreement, enumerations, reachability, violating edges and decidable failing-edge search, plus binary and rary affine classifications and counter observations.
